synthesis.summary: The panel converges on two structural concerns and several smaller hygiene issues. The ALTER TABLE refactor that removes the outer Delimited wrapper is flagged by five of six reviewers as a contract narrowing that silently drops support for comma-chained heterogeneous alterations, with the supporting fixture deleted as "invalid" without citation. The IdentityGrammar change for negative seeds is flagged by five reviewers as over-broad: it opens both seed and increment to optional signs as two independent tokens rather than via a single SignedNumericLiteral abstraction, and the test set only exercises a negative seed. Smaller issues — an unjustified NumericLiteralSegment branch in DEFAULT_LANGUAGE, missing boundary fixtures, and the patch bundling four unrelated features — round out the consensus. The CREATE LOGIN and table-variable-index additions are accepted as mechanically reasonable.

issues.description: ALTER TABLE lost its outer Delimited wrapper, narrowing the accepted language and silently dropping multi-action support
issues.detail: The previous grammar wrapped the OneOf in Delimited(...), permitting ALTER TABLE t ADD ..., DROP COLUMN ..., DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS ... in a single statement. The new grammar replaces this with a bare OneOf, so each ALTER TABLE accepts exactly one top-level action, and the fixture that exercised the chained form was deleted as 'invalid' without a citation to MS docs. Either restore the outer Delimited or cite the spec and add a negative-parse fixture asserting the wider form is rejected, plus a literate comment stating the invariant.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar admits a stray sign on the increment and leaks two-token sign representation through the parse tree
issues.detail: The patch adds Ref('SignedSegmentGrammar', optional=True) independently before both numeric literals, so seed and increment are each opened to a sign as two separate optional tokens. The stated motivation is negative seeds only, and the only fixture is IDENTITY(-2147483648, 1). Introduce a single SignedNumericLiteral abstraction (sign fused to its numeric literal) used in both positions so the parse tree presents one signed value to downstream rules, and add a fixture (e.g., IDENTITY(1, -1)) if signed increment is actually intended.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE silently gained a NumericLiteralSegment branch with no test, citation, or rationale
issues.detail: The _default_language OneOf was widened to accept NumericLiteralSegment alongside QuotedLiteralSegment and NakedIdentifierSegment. The PR description mentions only the unquoted-identifier case, and the new create_login.sql fixture exercises only DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=us_english. Either add a fixture for the numeric LCID form with a citation to the T-SQL spec, or drop NumericLiteralSegment to keep the grammar tight.

issues.description: Patch bundles four unrelated T-SQL grammar features in one diff
issues.detail: The PR mixes table-variable indexes in DECLARE, CREATE LOGIN identifier/nstring changes, signed IDENTITY seed, and the ALTER TABLE multi-DROP refactor. Each can regress independently and a future bisect will be painful. Split into separate commits or PRs so each landed change is reviewable and revertable on its own.

issues.description: New fixtures cover only happy paths; missing negative tests and boundary cases for the changed grammars
issues.detail: There is no parse-failure fixture asserting that the now-rejected multi-action ALTER TABLE form is rejected, no IDENTITY fixture with a signed increment, no mixed COLUMN+CONSTRAINT DROP, and no inline-column-index plus table-level-index combination in one DECLARE. Without negative tests at the new boundary, a future refactor could silently re-widen the grammar without detection. Add boundary fixtures so the accepted language is locked down on both sides.
